_why: A column's scale was never written down anywhere. Database-wide there are only five CHECK constraints mentioning confidence, and they use three different scales (1-5, 0-1, and a text enum); every other numeric column is undeclared. Nothing stopped a 0-1 producer and a 0-100 producer writing the same column, and nothing stopped a ten-year return percentage being stored as a 1-5 analyst rating for five months. This file is that missing declaration. It is deliberately data, not code, so a scale can be reviewed and corrected without a deploy.
_how_to_use: scripts/data_plausibility_monitor.py reads this, measures every declared column against its contract, and reports violations. It never writes to the tables it checks. A violation is not automatically a defect -- it may mean the contract is wrong -- but an undeclared, unmeasured column is how the Finviz shift survived 131,050 rows.
_severity: BLOCK means the value cannot be valid on its declared scale and a consumer acting on it is acting on fiction. WARN means implausible but conceivable, and wants a human look.

window_policy._why: 2026-10-18: range/min/max/finite/single_scale contracts measured the WHOLE table, so a row that went bad months ago (and was already quarantined or is frozen history) kept the contract violating forever and the daily run alerted every day. A contract is about what is being written NOW. Each windowed contract measures the last default_window_days by its window_column (explicit per contract), else the first of window_column_candidates the table actually has (information_schema); a table with none is measured whole and the detail says so. window_days: 0 on a contract opts it out.

alert_policy._why: 2026-10-18: the alert fingerprint carried raw violation counts, so a count that moved by one row was a 'changed finding set' and re-alerted daily. The fingerprint is now (table.column:rule) -> severity:band; a column that starts or stops violating, changes severity, or crosses one of pct_bands_pct (percent of rows in the window) is news. min_realert_minutes is the heartbeat for an UNCHANGED open finding set: 10080 = weekly (the shared state machine default of 360 minutes made a daily monitor heartbeat every run). A steady violation is still restated, never silent forever.

contracts._why: Finviz 'Recom' is a 1-5 analyst scale. Anything off it is not a recommendation. This is the contract that would have caught the column shift on day one: 97.9% of rows violated it.
A stop price below zero is never valid at any price, for any instrument. 17 rows held negative stops, the newest 2026-09-06.
Six rows held 2,147,479,900 -- within rounding of int32 max. That is a sentinel or an overflow leaking into a percentage, not a spread.
266 rows store NaN in a numeric column. NaN propagates silently through every aggregate that touches it, so one bad row poisons a whole average without raising anything.
28 rows store nan. Same failure mode as symbol_profiles.ytd_return_pct.

MIXED SCALES IN ONE COLUMN: 2,305 rows in (0,1] and 915 rows above 1. Some producer writes 0.85 and another writes 85, into the same column, with no declared scale to arbitrate. Any consumer thresholding this is wrong for one population. The contract asserts only that a column must pick ONE scale -- it deliberately does not guess which, because guessing is what produced the defect.
464,089 rows in (0,1] and 18 above 1. The 18 are the anomaly here, not the 464,089.
4,462 rows above 1 and 12 in (0,1]. Here the minority is the 0-1 population -- the opposite of agent_recommendation_registry, which is exactly why a single global rule would be wrong.

RETIRED STORE (2026-10-18). The analyst-vote provider (Finnhub) died 2026-07-28 and was retired 2026-09-13 (config/data_source_authority.json analyst_opinion.retired_stores); every row since held payload = {} (18,772 by 2026-09-13, 100% empty). The former required_fields rule (max_empty_pct 50 over 30 days) therefore failed every day on frozen, known debt. scripts/asset_intelligence_pipeline.py mirror_to_db no longer inserts an empty analyst payload, and readers (api_v2 analyst map / pro-analyst detail, broker_proposal_intel) render the distribution as 'unavailable' (scripts/lib/analyst_vote_distribution.py). The contract now fails only if an EMPTY payload row is written on or after retired_at: the writer fix regressed.
Uniformly 0-100 across all 680 rows. Internally consistent, so declared as 0-100 rather than 'fixed'. Recorded here so the scale stops being implicit.
Uniformly 0-100 across 41 rows. Same reasoning as incubator_universe.
Range 32.1-77.4 across 3,066 rows: 0-100. An earlier sweep flagged this as '100% implausible' by assuming 0-1. The sweep's rule was wrong, not the data -- recorded so that mistake is not repeated.

_not_declared_yet: market_quotes.day_change_pct, schwab_basis_divergence.divergence_pct, strategy_backtest_results.max_drawdown_pct and market_quote_snapshots.spread_pct all carry extreme outliers (13,105%, 12,818%, 15,026%, 384,043%). They are NOT declared here because a penny stock or a thin spread can legitimately produce large percentages, and declaring a bound that has not been verified would manufacture false violations. They need a judgement call before they get a contract.
